comparisons.peer_summary: For matters where losses are probable or reasonably possible and estimable, Citigroup estimates that the reasonably possible unaccrued loss for these matters ranges up to approximately $1.3 billion in the aggregate as of December 31, 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America and Citigroup disclose an aggregate estimated range of reasonably possible loss for disclosed litigation and regulatory matters, noting that these estimates are based on currently available information and subject to significant judgment. However, the specific ranges differ: Citigroup estimates the reasonably possible unaccrued loss 'ranges up to approximately $1.3 billion' as of December 31, 2024, whereas Bank of America's estimated range is '$0 to $0.8 billion' in excess of accrued liabilities.

The accrued liability and estimated range of possible loss are based upon currently available information and subject to significant judgment, a variety of assumptions and known and unknown uncertainties.
For some of the matters disclosed below, Citigroup is currently able to estimate a reasonably possible loss or range of loss in excess of amounts accrued (if any).
These estimates are based on currently available information.

comparisons.peer_topic: Legal Proceedings Estimation Methodology and Liability
comparisons.peer_summary: The firm is involved in various judicial and regulatory proceedings, many in early stages with indeterminate damages. For estimable matters, the upper end of the reasonably possible loss range is estimated at approximately $1.7 billion in excess of aggregate reserves as of the filing date.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America and Goldman Sachs provide an estimated range of reasonably possible loss for legal proceedings, highlighting that many matters are in early stages or involve uncertainties. The estimated upper bound differs significantly: Goldman Sachs reports the upper end of the range is 'approximately $1.7 billion' in excess of aggregate reserves, while Bank of America reports an upper bound of '$0 to $0.8 billion'. Both firms also note that these estimates involve significant judgment and are based on currently available information.

sentences.text: For any matter disclosed in this Note for which a loss in future periods is reasonably possible and estimable (whether in excess of an accrued liability or where there is no accrued liability), the Corporation's estimated range of possible loss is $0 to $0.8 billion in excess of the accrued liability, if any, as of December 31, 2024.

The accrued liability and estimated range of possible loss are based upon currently available information and subject to significant judgment, a variety of assumptions and known and unknown uncertainties.

Under ASC 450, an event is "reasonably possible" if "the chance of the future event or events occurring is more than remote but less than likely" and an event is "remote" if "the chance of the future event or events occurring is slight." Thus, references to the upper end of the range of reasonably possible loss for cases in which the firm is able to estimate a range of reasonably possible loss mean the upper end of the range of loss for cases for which the firm believes the risk of loss is more than slight.
Many of these proceedings are in early stages, and many of these cases seek an indeterminate amount of damages.

comparisons.peer_topic: Litigation Reserve Policy and Aggregate Estimated Losses
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024, the Firm estimates the aggregate range of reasonably possible losses for legal proceedings to be $0 to approximately $1.4 billion, noting that estimates involve significant judgment due to the number, stages, and uncertainty of proceedings. The Firm accrues litigation liabilities under U.S. GAAP when probable and estimable, adjusting quarterly based on counsel consultation, having incurred $740 million in legal expenses in 2024, though future adjustments are not assured given the difficulty in predicting outcomes.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America and JPMorgan Chase disclose an aggregate range of reasonably possible losses for legal proceedings, acknowledging that estimates involve significant judgment due to the unpredictable nature of such matters. JPMorgan Chase estimates the range is '$0 to approximately $1.4 billion', which is higher than Bank of America's '$0 to $0.8 billion'. Both firms state that actual losses may vary significantly from these current estimates.

sentences.text: For any matter disclosed in this Note for which a loss in future periods is reasonably possible and estimable (whether in excess of an accrued liability or where there is no accrued liability), the Corporation's estimated range of possible loss is $0 to $0.8 billion in excess of the accrued liability, if any, as of December 31, 2024.

The matters underlying the accrued liability and estimated range of possible loss are unpredictable and may change from time to time, and actual losses may vary significantly from the current estimate and accrual.

The Firm believes the estimate of the aggregate range of reasonably possible losses, in excess of reserves established, for its legal proceedings is from $0 to approximately $1.4 billion at December 31, 2024.
Accordingly, the Firm's estimate of the aggregate range of reasonably possible losses will change from time to time, and actual losses may vary significantly.

comparisons.peer_topic: Difficulty in estimating legal loss contingencies
comparisons.peer_summary: It is often difficult to determine if a loss is probable or reasonably possible, or to estimate the amount, particularly when factual records are contested, damages are substantial or indeterminate, or novel legal questions arise.
comparisons.comparison: While Bank of America provides a specific estimated range of possible loss ($0 to $0.8 billion), Morgan Stanley emphasizes the inherent difficulty in determining or estimating loss amounts, particularly when factual records are contested or damages are indeterminate. This highlights a divergence in disclosure specificity: Bank of America quantifies its exposure range, whereas Morgan Stanley focuses on the uncertainty factors that make estimation difficult, though both operate within the same litigation and regulatory contingency framework.

sentences.text: For any matter disclosed in this Note for which a loss in future periods is reasonably possible and estimable (whether in excess of an accrued liability or where there is no accrued liability), the Corporation's estimated range of possible loss is $0 to $0.8 billion in excess of the accrued liability, if any, as of December 31, 2024.
In many legal proceedings and investigations, it is inherently difficult to determine whether any loss is probable or reasonably possible, or to estimate the amount of any loss.

In addition, even where the Firm has determined that a loss is probable or reasonably possible or an exposure to loss or range of loss exists in excess of the liability already accrued with respect to a previously recognized loss contingency, the Firm may be unable to reasonably estimate the amount of the loss or range of loss.
